title: Garba dancers can circle a lamp inside a clay pot
body: In the traditional Garba of Gujarat, dancers move anticlockwise around a central image of the goddess Amba or a perforated earthen pot containing an oil lamp. UNESCO listed the dance tradition in 2023.
takeaway: The centre gives a roomful of dancers the same point to orient around.
source: UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage, Garba of Gujarat (2023)
visual: an overhead view of a circle of dancers around a lit clay pot

title: Rajasthan's Kalbelia dance evokes the movements of snakes
body: Kalbelia women dance in flowing black skirts and mimic a serpent's movements. Musicians may play the poongi, a wind instrument associated with the community's former work as snake handlers.
takeaway: A performance can carry traces of an occupation even when people have found new ways to make a living.
source: UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage, Kalbelia Folk Songs and Dances (2010)
visual: a dancer in a flowing dark skirt turning beside seated musicians

title: Four countries jointly nominated the tradition of making couscous
body: Algeria, Mauritania, Morocco and Tunisia jointly submitted couscous traditions to UNESCO. The 2020 listing covers skills such as rolling semolina into grains and steaming them to cook.
takeaway: A food can be shared across borders while households keep their own ways of serving it.
source: UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage, Couscous Production and Consumption (2020)
visual: hands rolling semolina into grains over a wide shallow platter
